Subject: Dedicated capacity recap - Helium Health

Hi Asha / Hector -

Thanks again for the call earlier - really helpful to hear about the integrations and traffic profile. Below is a quick recap of what we heard and the recommended next steps so we're aligned heading into the proposal.

Summary of pain points / goals
- Latency spikes during morning sync windows causing timeouts for clinical workflows.
- Strict data isolation requirement for PHI; must run in a customer-dedicated environment with VPC isolation and encryption at rest.
- Need predictable throughput for inference (initial sustained ~150-200 reqs/s, peak bursts to ~350 reqs/s).
- Budget sensitivity: prefer a phased approach to reduce upfront commitment while locking predictable unit costs.

Recommended Dedicated capacity plan (high level)
- Reserved capacity: start with 4x A100-equivalent GPUs dedicated (reserved) for baseline throughput.
- Burst/scale: autoscale/burst up to 8 GPUs for predictable peak windows.
- Isolation: VPC + tenant-only capacity, optional on-prem connector later if required by security.
- SLA targets: 99.9% availability for the dedicated pool; P95 generation latency target < 200ms for typical prompt lengths (we'll validate against your prompt set).
- Cost optimization: KV/prefix caching and batching recommended for nightly syncs to reduce per-token cost.

Action items / next steps
1) I attached an updated proposal (helium_health_dedicated_proposal_v2.pdf) and a capacity plan (capacity_plan_2027.xlsx) - please review.
2) Can you confirm procurement contact and preferred billing cadence? (You mentioned annual preferred.)
3) Would you like us to provision a 2-week pilot (4 GPUs) while you run your eval prompts, then convert to reserved 4 -> 8 based on telemetry?
4) Technical deep-dive: Rishi / Dev can set a joint call early next week to go over network/firewall, IAM, and SSO requirements.

If that captures everything I heard, I'll follow up with a refined timeline (provisioning and onboarding) and an updated pricing sheet tied to the pilot vs reserved commitment.

Thanks -
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa / Asha - quick technical notes ahead of Tue's deep-dive. Pasting the recommended configuration and risk items so procurement/InfoSec have context.

Recommended baseline
- Reserved pool: 4x A100-class GPUs (reserved nodes) in a dedicated VPC.
- Burst: allow autoscaling burst to 8x GPUs for scheduled peak windows (supports your 350 reqs/s peak).
- Instance sizing: mix of 1x8B-optimized and 3x16B-inference instances depending on model family; we'll confirm after prompt set run.
- Caching: enable KV/prefix caching for nightly batch syncs to drop token compute by ~45% in our tests.

SLA and telemetry
- Target SLA: 99.9% availability for the reserved pool; SLO for P95 generation latency < 200ms on standard prompts.
- Telemetry: we'll provide token-level cost, per-route latency histograms, and 24/7 tracing hooks for the pilot.

Network / security notes for InfoSec
- Connectivity: VPC peering and customer-managed subnets. Support for private endpoints and egress controls.
- Data handling: all PHI remains in the dedicated pool; encryption at rest with customer KMS, and optional HSM for keys.
- Evidence pack: SOC2 summary, architecture diagram, and network checklist attached. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-hel-health-arch

Provisioning timeline (estimates)
- Pilot provisioning (4 GPUs): 3-5 business days after signed pilot agreement.
- Full reserved conversion & onboarding: 7-10 business days post-signature depending on requested region and capacity constraints.

Open risks / questions
- If Helium requires on-prem or air-gapped deployment for PHI, that adds ~3-4 weeks to timeline and a different licensing model.
- Need confirmation on expected prompt lengths (tokens) and concurrency patterns to finalize instance sizing.

Attachments: SOC2_summary_2027.pdf (stub), network_arch_diagram_v2.pdf (stub)

I'll join Tue 7/6 09:30 SGT. Let me know if you want a pre-brief with InfoSec folks beforehand.
